title: Officina configuration
description: Generated from the Options classes of Sleepyshark.Officina.Core; see docs/configuration-settings.md.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema of the file, for editor completion. Files only.

formatVersion.description: The configuration format version. Unknown versions are rejected.

project.description: The project's identity, and values usable in placeholders.

name.description: The project's name. Usable in instructions as `{{project.name}}`.

values.description: Free-form text values. Usable in instructions as `{{project.values.<name>}}`.

apiKey.description: The provider's credential, as the name of a secret, which is read when it is used.

secret.description: The name of the secret, such as the environment variable that holds it. Required.

prices.description: Prices per million tokens, by model id, for reporting cost and enforcing cost budgets. A model without a price costs nothing.

cacheRead.description: USD per million tokens read from the cache.

cacheWrite.description: USD per million tokens written to the cache.

models.description: Model profiles, by name. Agents refer to them by name.

provider.description: The provider that serves this profile, by its name in `providers`. Required.

effort.description: Reasoning effort, such as `low`, `medium` or `high`. Unset uses the provider's default.

maxOutputTokens.description: The most tokens one reply may have. Unset uses the provider's default.

toolChoice.description: Whether the model may call tools.

settings.description: Any other setting the provider declares for the model, such as a temperature, as text.

extends.description: Another agent definition this one builds on: it inherits every setting it does not set itself. Files only.

description.description: What the agent is for. Usable in instructions as `{{agent.description}}`.

instructions.description: The agent's job. Only the application knows it, so it has no default. Placeholders may use the project and the agent only. Required.
examples: Extract the invoice number, date and total. Reply as JSON.

model.description: The name of the model profile the agent runs on. Required.

triggers.description: How work may reach the agent: `conversation`, `request`, `batch`, `schedule`, `event` or `longRunning`. Work that arrives any other way is rejected. Unset accepts every way.

tools.description: The tool sets, by name in `toolSets`, whose tools the agent is offered. The same tools are offered whoever the caller is.

toolDescriptionsOnDemand.description: Whether the model is offered only the tools' names, and reads a tool's description and arguments with `describe_tool` when it needs them. For agents with many tools.

permissions.description: Narrows the caller's permissions for this agent's tool calls: a permission counts only if the caller holds it and it is listed here. Unset keeps the caller's.

maxParallelToolCalls.description: The most tool calls from one reply that run at the same time, when every tool called is safe to run in parallel.

context.description: How the agent's model input is built. Required.

operatingFacts.description: Facts added after the history for every model call, in this order, such as limits or the date. Placeholders may use `{{now}}` and `{{now:date}}`, and the project and agent values.

historyCacheLifetime.description: How long the provider keeps the conversation cached between model calls, as `hh:mm:ss`, at most one hour. Agents that often wait for approvals benefit from longer.

retrieval.description: Knowledge retrieved before each turn. Required.

beforeTurn.description: Knowledge sources, by name in `knowledge`, searched with the turn's work before the turn starts. Their passages are given to the model as data in the volatile context.

handOffWhenNotCovered.description: Whether the turn ends in a handoff for a policy gap, without calling the model, when no source searched before the turn covers the work.

history.description: What history a request starts with, and how it is shortened. Required.

strategy.description: `none`: each request starts a new conversation. `full`: the agent's conversation with the caller continues, and is never shortened, so once it is too long for the model the turn is handed off. `shortened`: it continues, and is shortened once when the model reports it too long. `lastTurns`: it continues with the last `lastTurns` turns only. All but `none` need the conversation store.

shortening.description: How `shortened` history is shortened: `provider` by the model provider's own mechanism, or `extension:<id>` by a shortener the application registers. The current turn is never shortened. Required.

lastTurns.description: For `lastTurns`: how many earlier turns a request starts with.

stopWhen.description: When a turn is complete. They combine: the first that holds completes the turn. Required.

finished.description: The turn completes when the model finishes its reply. When this is `false` and the model finishes, the turn ends in a handoff.

finishTool.description: A tool, by name in `tools`, that completes the turn when a call of it succeeds. The call's arguments are the output.

maxIterations.description: The turn completes after this many model calls, with the model's last text as the output.

budget.description: The agent's budgets. They can be high, but they cannot be removed or unlimited. Required.

turn.description: The limits of each turn, checked before every model call. A turn that reaches one ends in a handoff. Required.

iterations.description: The most model calls in a turn.

toolCalls.description: The most tool calls in a turn, including tools the provider runs itself.

tokens.description: The most tokens a turn may use: input, output, cache reads and cache writes together.

cost.description: The most a turn may spend, in USD.

time.description: The longest a turn may take, as `hh:mm:ss`.

stall.description: When a turn has stalled. Required.

iterationsWithoutProgress.description: A turn ends in a handoff after this many tool-calling iterations in a row that only repeat earlier calls and get the same results.

handOffOnPolicyGap.description: Whether a turn ends in a handoff for a policy gap when every tool call of an iteration is refused. With `false`, the refusals go back to the model.

toolServers.description: External tool servers (MCP), by name. Tools use their tools with `mcp:<server>/<tool>` sources.

transport.description: How the server is reached: `stdio` starts `command` and talks over its standard input and output; `http` posts to `url` (Streamable HTTP).

command.description: For `stdio`: the program that runs the server.

env.description: For `stdio`: environment variables of the program, each a secret read when the server starts.

secret.description: The name of the secret, such as the environment variable that holds it. Required.

headers.description: For `http`: headers sent with every request, each a secret read when the server is first reached.

tools.description: Tools, by the name the model sees.

source.description: Where the tool comes from: `extension:<id>` for a tool the application registers, `mcp:<server>/<tool>` for a tool of a server in `toolServers`, `knowledge:<name>` to search a source in `knowledge`, or `provider:<name>` for a tool the model provider runs itself. Required.

kind.description: `write` for a tool that changes something. Unset uses the tool's declaration, and `write` for a tool server's tools; a tool that declares itself `write` stays `write`.

permissions.description: Permissions the caller must hold to call the tool.

gates.description: The tool's own gates, by name in `gates`. They run after the gates for all tools.

gateExemption.description: Why a write tool needs no gate of its own. Every write tool needs gates or this reason.
examples: Writes only to a scratch folder.

approval.description: Whether each call needs a human's approval. Unset means `always` for irreversible tools, otherwise `never`. For approval by rule, give the tool a `builtin:require-approval` gate with a condition.

timeout.description: The longest one call may take, as `hh:mm:ss`.

maxAttempts.description: How many times a call is tried. Only timeouts and unavailable errors are retried, and irreversible tools never are.

maxResultLength.description: The most characters of a result that enter the conversation; the rest is cut off.

parallelSafe.description: Whether calls may run at the same time as other calls. Unset uses the tool's declaration; `true` cannot loosen a tool that declares itself unsafe. Irreversible tools never run in parallel.

irreversible.description: Whether the tool's effects cannot be undone. Such a tool is a write tool, is carried out at most once for the same run and arguments, and needs approval unless `approval` says otherwise.

maskResults.description: Whether personal data in the tool's results is masked before the model sees them, when masking is on.

receivesMaskedValues.description: Whether masked values are restored in the tool's arguments, so it receives the real ones, such as a tool that sends an email. Its results are masked again.

untrusted.description: Whether the tool's results are untrusted content, such as fetched web pages. An agent that has read them is marked, and gates can act on the mark.

reason.description: Why a provider tool is enabled. Required for `provider:` tools.

toolSets.description: Named groups of tools, by name in `tools`. Agents are offered tools by tool set.

gates.description: Gates, by name. Tools and policies refer to them by name.

use.description: What the gate runs: `builtin:require-approval` or `builtin:deny`, which act when `when` holds; `builtin:untrusted-content-approval`, which asks when `when` holds and the agent has read untrusted content; or `extension:<id>` for a gate the application registers. Required.

when.description: For the built-in gates: the condition over the tool's arguments under which the gate acts. Unset means always.

field.description: The field a test reads: a dotted path with optional `[n]` indexes, such as `args.branch`.

is.description: Holds when the field equals this value. Numbers compare by value, and `true` and `false` match booleans.

in.description: Holds when the field equals one of these values.

gt.description: Holds when the field is a number greater than this.

gte.description: Holds when the field is a number greater than or equal to this.

lt.description: Holds when the field is a number less than this.

lte.description: Holds when the field is a number less than or equal to this.

exists.description: `true` holds when the field is present and not null; `false` when it is missing or null.

all.description: Holds when every one of these conditions holds.

policies.description: Permission rules, gates for all tools, anonymous callers' permissions, masking and rate limits.

permissionRules.description: Permission rules, in order. The first that matches a call decides it; a call no rule matches goes on.

tool.description: The tool the rule applies to, by name in `tools`. Required.

when.description: The condition over the tool's arguments under which the rule matches, written as in `gates.<name>.when`. Unset matches every call.

lt.description: Holds when the field is a number less than this.

lte.description: Holds when the field is a number less than or equal to this.

not.description: Holds when this condition does not.

action.description: What a match decides: `allow`, `deny`, `ask` a human, or `route` to `to`.

reason.description: Why, as told to the model and the human.

to.description: For `route`: the agent, by name, that the turn is handed to.

gates.description: Gates, by name in `gates`, that run before every tool call, ahead of the tool's own gates.

anonymousPermissions.description: The permissions a caller without an identity holds.

masking.description: Masking of personal data in work from outside, before the model, history or logs see it. On by default. Required.

enabled.description: Whether masking is on. Turn it off where it would corrupt the content, such as source code.

patterns.description: What is masked: regular expressions by name, which replace the built-in ones for email addresses, phone numbers and payment card numbers. Each match becomes a token such as `[email-1]`, the same for the same value throughout the run. Names may use letters, digits and underscores.

rateLimits.description: How much work each owner and each tenant may send. Required.

perOwner.description: The limit for each owner. Anonymous callers share one. No limit when unset.

permits.description: How many work items are admitted in each window.

window.description: How long a window lasts, as `hh:mm:ss`.

perTenant.description: The limit for each tenant. Callers without a tenant share one. No limit when unset.

permits.description: How many work items are admitted in each window.

window.description: How long a window lasts, as `hh:mm:ss`.

use.description: The source the application registers, as `extension:<id>`. Required.

mask.description: Whether personal data in the passages is masked before the model sees them, when masking is on.

budget.description: The run's budget. It can be high, but it cannot be removed or unlimited. Required. Live: the owner may change it during a run.

cost.description: The most the run may spend, in USD. Live: the owner may change it during a run.

time.description: The longest the run may take, as `hh:mm:ss` or `d.hh:mm:ss`. Live: the owner may change it during a run.

permissionMode.description: How tool calls that need permission are decided: `ask` the owner, `auto` by the rules, or `readOnly`. Live: the owner may change it during a run.

telemetry.description: Measurements and the warnings raised from them. Required.

cacheHitWarning.description: The share of a model call's input read from the provider's cache, from 0 to 1, below which a warning is raised. The first call of a turn is not checked.

storage.description: What is stored, and for how long.

unstoredEvents.description: Kinds of event that are published live but not stored, so a reader that joins late or falls behind does not see them. Unset leaves out streamed text only: storing each piece slows the agent, and the conversation keeps the text.

retention.description: How long each kind of stored data is kept. Runs, conversations and events without a period are kept until they are deleted.

runs.description: How long a run, with the configuration it used, is kept after it starts, as `d.hh:mm:ss`.

events.description: How long an event is kept after it happens, as `d.hh:mm:ss`.

conversations.description: How long a turn of a stored conversation is kept after it ends, as `d.hh:mm:ss`. Once its earliest turns are deleted, a conversation continues from the turns kept.

audit.description: How long an audit entry is kept after it is written, as `d.hh:mm:ss`. A request to delete an owner's data leaves audit entries to this period.

capabilities.description: Optional capabilities and their settings. All are off by default.

conversationStore.description: The conversation store: each agent's conversation with each caller is kept, anonymous callers sharing one, so a history strategy other than `none` continues it across requests and restarts.

knowledge.description: Knowledge retrieval: the sources in `knowledge`, searched before a turn or through `knowledge:` tools.

workspace.description: The git workspace: a working copy per agent, and an integration queue into the baseline.

protectedPaths.description: Paths agents cannot see or change, in addition to the fixed ones: `.git`, `**/.env*` and `.sof/**` are hidden, and `sof.json` and `sof.*.json` are read-only.

path.description: A glob relative to the workspace root, where `**` matches any number of folders. Required.

access.description: `hidden`: agents cannot see it at all; `readOnly`: they can read it but not change it.

keepWorkingCopies.description: Whether an agent's working copy is kept when its task ends, so the owner can look at it.

sandbox.description: The sandbox that commands run in: no network unless allowed, and command rules. It needs the workspace.

allowedHosts.description: The hosts commands may reach, through a filtering proxy. `*.` matches any subdomain. Empty means no network.

commandRules.description: Rules for commands, in order. Each command of a command line is decided by the first rule that matches it, and the strictest decision applies. A command no rule matches is asked about.

match.description: The command it applies to, where `*` matches any text and `?` any one character. Required.

action.description: What a match decides: `allow`, `ask` a human, or `deny`.

secrets.description: The secrets each agent's commands receive as environment variables, by agent name. Other agents' commands never see them.
